forms-quiz-structure.title: Identify sound form structure
forms-quiz-structure.prompt: Which two statements describe useful form structure?
forms-quiz-structure.hint: Think about grouping and label connections.

help.concept: Forms group related controls, and labels should identify the controls they describe.
help.hint_1: One correct statement is about the form boundary.
help.hint_2: The other is about matching for and id values.

options.a: Place controls for one submission inside a form element.
options.b: Match a label's for value to the related control's id.
options.c: Use a heading instead of a label for every input.
options.d: Give every input the same id so labels are easier to write.

help.concept: A labeled control belongs inside its form boundary.
help.hint_1: The label can come before the input.
help.hint_2: The matching for/id connection appears before the closing form.

form-groups-controls.title: Use form to group controls that belong to one submission
form-groups-controls.bodyMarkdown:
A `<form>` groups the controls that belong to one user submission. The form element describes the boundary of the interaction; the controls inside it collect the values.

```html
<form>
  <label for="student-name">Name</label>
  <input id="student-name" name="student_name" type="text">
</form>
```

Read this example line by line: `form` opens the form region, the label names the field, the input collects the value, and the closing `form` ends the group. For this course, the browser preview shows the form itself; no server is required.

explicit-label-connection.title: Match label for with the control id
explicit-label-connection.bodyMarkdown:
A visible label should be programmatically connected to its control. Give the input an `id`, then use that same value in the label's `for` attribute. This makes the label useful to mouse, touch, keyboard, and assistive-technology users.

```html
<label for="email">Email address</label>
<input id="email" name="email" type="email">
```

Read the example line by line: the label points to `email`, the input owns `id="email"`, and the matching values create the connection. The `name` identifies the value when form data is submitted.
